clue.text: Trim tree

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart
a conifer, a kind of evergreen tree

explanation.definitionFit: Spruce is both an adjective for neat, smart appearance and the name of a common evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Winger short of very big game

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a winger is a bird, here the osprey
OS stands for outsize, very big in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A wing player falls short of landing really large game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird. 'short of' removes OS from OSPREY. 'big game' looks like the definition; only 'game' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey are hunted animals, the quarry a hunter pursues, which is what game means.

clue.text: Amazing party after try a French fellow secured

indicators.note: secured means held firmly, so the outer pieces hold the inner ones between them

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: after places the party piece following the try piece

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Frenchman scores a rugby try and then has a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' suggests rugby but means hear a case in court; 'secured' wraps the French article and the fellow around the rest, and 'after' fixes the order inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard-of has never happened before, so it is remarkable, extraordinary.

clue.text: European left Yankee union for the stage

parts.note: to have left is to have quit
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A European walks out on an American trade union for actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the trade union representing actors and performers in Britain.

clue.text: Check out underground laboratory item

parts.note: to check something out is to test it
the Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone is told to inspect a piece of kit in a basement lab.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway system.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is the narrow glass vessel used for holding samples in chemistry experiments.

clue.text: How obtuse adult and radical ruined TV nature series

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A grumble that a dim grown-up and an extremist spoiled a wildlife programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges HOW OBTUSE ADULT plus R. The World About Us was a long-running BBC documentary strand.
explanation.definitionFit: The World About Us was a BBC television documentary series about wildlife and natural history.

clue.text: A representative visiting county's plant by the sea

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: a shire is an English county; the 's is a link meaning has
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An MP on a constituency visit stops to admire a coastal plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' sends the representative into the county; shire survives in English county names such as Yorkshire and Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Samphire is a fleshy, edible plant that grows on coastal rocks and salt marshes.

clue.text: RA's equipment fails

definitions.meaning: armoured fighting vehicles, kit of the army; RA is the Royal Artillery
to tank is informal for to flop, to fail badly

explanation.definitionFit: Tanks are armoured military vehicles, and tanks as a verb means flops or collapses.

clue.text: Subject: 'The Dance of Iconic Bees'

indicators.note: a dance moves bodies around, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A lecture title on how famous bees perform their waggle dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance' looks like part of a title, as bees really do dance, but it signals rearranging ICONIC BEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bioscience is a field of academic study, the life sciences, a subject on a curriculum.

clue.text: Shed many layers here

parts.note: reads like peeling off clothing, but a shed is a hut and layers are egg-laying hens kept in it

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip off several layers of clothing in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb meaning take off, but it is a noun, a small outbuilding; 'layers' are hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultry coop is a small outbuilding where egg-laying birds are kept, so it is a shed full of layers.

clue.text: Fish bar cut sandwiches

indicators.note: something that sandwiches another holds it between its two halves, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to mow grass is to cut it
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A fish bar's menu is pared down to sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish bar' reads as one place, but the clue splits there: 'Fish' is the definition and 'bar' starts the wordplay, which 'sandwiches' closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a small freshwater species of the carp family, a tiny fish.

clue.text: Study classics, bar first quarter, collecting cup

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the shortened word takes the other piece inside itself
bar means except; the first quarter of the eight-letter word classics is its opening two letters, which go

parts.note: a cup is a trophy awarded to a winner

explanation.surface: Someone studies the classics, skipping the early part, while winning a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar first quarter' drops two of the eight letters, leaving ASSICS; 'collecting' then takes the cup inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrophysics is a branch of science, a field of academic study concerned with the physics of stars.

clue.text: Dominant priest ranting about English version of bible

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ranting word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: railing means complaining loudly, ranting
V is the abbreviation for version, as in the bible's Authorised Version

explanation.surface: A clergyman raves about an English translation of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E and V inside RAILING after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A prevailing view or wind is the one most widespread or strongest, so it is dominant.

clue.text: Like conditions in the Kalahari desert

definitions.text: Like conditions in the Kalahari desert

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A description of the climate in southern Africa's great sandy wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is tucked inside 'KalahARI Desert', and the whole clue is also its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari receives very little rain, so its climate is dry, parched and waterless.

clue.text: Flyer allowed to cover old Republican president

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: allowed means let
R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight D. Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Permission to give cover to an elderly Republican leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' wraps the permission word around the rest. Eisenhower, known as Ike, really was a Republican president, so the surface holds together.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorikeet is a small brightly coloured parrot, a bird, and so a flyer.

clue.text: Aggressive colonist's like rebel when disturbed

definitions.note: colonist's stands for colonist is, the 's working as a link

indicators.note: disturbed means jumbled out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fierce settler behaves like a rebel once stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when disturbed' rearranges LIKE REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer bees are an Africanised honeybee strain notorious for fierce swarming; bees live in colonies.

clue.text: Heading north, top-class coach skirts Polish residential area

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means going up the grid, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: A1 means top-class, written here as AI

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the outer pieces enclose it

parts.note: a coach is a bus
to polish is to rub

explanation.surface: A luxury coach heading north detours around Polish territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality but the verb. 'skirts' gives AIRUBBUS, which 'Heading north' turns round; A1 is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbia means the suburbs collectively, the housing districts on a city's outskirts.

clue.text: Endlessly ardent enthusiast, one hugging posh birds

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter, so the synonym is cut short

parts.note: ardent means avid, keen

indicators.note: hugging means holding close around, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: an enthusiast is a fan
U is the old British label for upper-class, posh usage
one is A, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A passionate fan clutches someone well-to-do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts AVID to AVI; 'hugging' puts U inside FAN to make FAUN. U for upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for the bird species of a region, its bird life.

clue.text: Lake of Caledonian highlands primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of each of these four words is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a body of water found mainly in Scotland's hilly north.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Lake, Of, Caledonian, Highlands spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it. Caledonia is Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is the Scottish word for a lake, found chiefly in the Highlands.

clue.text: Six clubs supported by one Peruvian wool supplier

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means placed underneath, so the last piece goes below the others

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
una is one in Spanish, the language of Peru

explanation.surface: Six golf clubs are propped up by a single Peruvian sheep farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts UNA below VI and C in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The vicuna is a wild Andean relative of the llama prized for its fine fleece.

clue.text: Dental assistant tried noxious compound

indicators.note: compound as a verb means mix together, so the letters of these two words are combined anew

explanation.surface: A dentist's helper experimented with a poisonous chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemistry noun, fitting the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange TRIED NOXIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gas is used by dentists as a mild anaesthetic, so it assists in dental work.

clue.text: Catch crawler in New York

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish, something an angler catches
American slang for cockroach, a scuttling insect

explanation.definitionFit: A roach is a fish an angler lands, and in American slang a roach is a cockroach.

clue.text: Typical of 15s beside American lodging

indicators.note: lodging means staying inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: by means beside, next to

explanation.surface: An American stays in lodgings beside a beehive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodging' tucks one piece into the other. 15s refers to 15 down, the killer bees: bees are proverbially busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees are proverbially hard-working, as in the saying 'busy as a bee', so busy is characteristic of them.

clue.text: One wheels in books for baker's agent

indicators.note: in signals that the first pieces go inside the other one

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book, so BB is books
I is the Roman numeral one
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: Someone drives into a pile of books while out on a delivery for a baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts one and wheels between the two book letters; wheels is everyday slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a raising agent used by bakers to make cakes rise.

clue.text: Basque occasionally blocks strike approval

indicators.note: something that blocks another sits in its way, in the middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: to strike is to thump

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Basque protester stops a strike from getting the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but means hit; 'occasionally' takes alternate letters of Basque and 'blocks' sets them in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised-thumb gesture is a sign of agreement or approval.

clue.text: After, say, golf, he notices experts

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
notices are adverts, ads

explanation.surface: After a round of golf, a man spots some specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link that lets the surface read as a sentence; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is an informal word for intellectuals, clever people who know a lot about a subject.

clue.text: Malagasy primate votes in the affirmative

definitions.meaning: a nocturnal lemur found only in Madagascar
aye is a yes vote, so two of them are two votes in favour

explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a lemur of Madagascar, and aye is the parliamentary word for yes.
